aiOverview.content: At the 98th Academy Awards on March 15, 2026, a rare tie occurred in the Best Live Action Short Film category between "The Singers" and "Two People Exchanging Saliva," marking the seventh tie in Oscar history. Ties are extremely uncommon, with previous instances including Best Actress in 1969 and Sound Editing in 2013. This video shows the moment the tie was announced at the 2026 Oscars:00:40ABC7YouTube • Mar 15, 2026 00:40 Here are the confirmed ties in Academy Awards history: 2026 (98th): Best Live Action Short Film – "The Singers" (Sam Davis) and "Two People Exchanging Saliva" (Natalie Musteata and Alexandre Singh). 2013 (85th): Best Sound Editing – Skyfall and Zero Dark Thirty. 1995 (67th): Best Short Film (Live Action) – Trevor and Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life. 1987 (59th): Best Documentary (Feature) – Artie Shaw: Time Is All You've Got and Down and Out in America. 1969 (41st): Best Actress – Katharine Hepburn (The Lion in Winter) and Barbra Streisand (Funny Girl). 1950 (22nd): Best Documentary (Short Subject) – A Chance to Live and So Much for So Little. 1932 (5th): Best Actor – Wallace Beery (The Champ) and Fredric March (Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde). Key Facts About Oscar Ties The 1932 Rule Change: In 1932, Wallace Beery actually had one fewer vote than Fredric March, but the rules at the time stated that anyone within three votes of the winner also received an award. Following this, the Academy changed the rules to require an exact match in votes. Most Famous Tie: The 1969 Best Actress tie between Barbra Streisand and Katharine Hepburn is widely considered the most famous, as it is the only time a tie has occurred in a major acting category. Handling the Moment: When a tie occurs, both recipients are typically invited onto the stage, either together or in quick succession, to receive their awards. At the 2026 Oscars, presenter Kumail Nanjiani handled the surprise by inviting the first winner up, followed by the second.
